[ASSISTANT_SAID] Francisco Franco collaborated with notable composers, including Manuel Parada and Juan Quintero.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Manuel Parada scored several of Franco's films during the 1940s and 1950s, emphasizing nationalistic themes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Juan Quintero composed music for several of Franco's films, including "Los ojos dejan huellas" (1942) and "Raza" (1944).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Franco's regime heavily censored the film industry, forcing many artists into collaboration out of necessity.  
[USER] User asked if any Spanish filmmakers during Franco's time made films that were critical of his regime.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some Spanish filmmakers did create films critical of Franco's regime, despite pervasive censorship.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "El verdugo" (The Executioner) by Luis García Berlanga was a disguised critique of Franco's regime.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "El verdugo" faced severe censorship and was forbidden to be shown until several years later.
